source.author: verg
source.text: Tum pudor incendit vires et conscia virtus, praecipitemque Daren ardens agit aequore toto, nunc dextra ingeminans ictus, nunc ille sinistra; nec mora, nec requies: quam multa grandine nimbi culminibus crepitant, sic densis ictibus heros creber utraque manu pulsat versatque Dareta.
source.text_original: Tum pudor incendit vires et conscia virtus, / praecipitemque Daren ardens agit aequore toto, / nunc dextra ingeminans ictus, nunc ille sinistra; / nec mora, nec requies: quam multa grandine nimbi / culminibus crepitant, sic densis ictibus heros / creber utraque manu pulsat versatque Dareta.
source.text_english: Then shame and conscious valor kindle his strength, and blazing he drives Dares headlong over the whole plain, now redoubling blows with his right hand, now with his left; there is no delay, no rest: as often as storm clouds rattle on rooftops with hail, so the hero, with dense blows from either hand, beats and buffets Dares.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: quam multa leo cunctatus in arta mole virum rictuque genas et lumina pressit, sic curae subiere ducem, ferrumne capessat imbelle atque aevi senior gestamina primi an patres regnique acuat mutabile vulgus.
reuse.text_original: quam multa leo cunctatus in arta / mole virum rictuque genas et lumina pressit, / sic curae subiere ducem, ferrumne capessat / imbelle atque aevi senior gestamina primi / an patres regnique acuat mutabile vulgus.
reuse.text_english: How long the lion, after delaying in the cramped mass, pressed the man’s cheeks and eyes with its jaws; so cares came over the leader, whether he should seize the sword, though unfit for war and now older than the burdens of his first age, or whether he should rouse the fathers and the changeable common people of the kingdom.
